questions.q: What is the sum of all the natural number between $1$ and $200$ which are multiple of $5$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Average Balancing)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... AP ka sum bina gande formula ke solve hota hai, sirf average ka hack laga.

Pen-Free Observation: Range $5$ se start hoke $195$ tak jayegi. Average lagbhag $100$ aayega aur numbers $40$ ke aas-paas hain. $100 \times 40 = 4000$ ke kareeb ka answer hoga.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): AP me Average hamesha $\frac{\text{First} + \text{Last}}{2}$ hota hai. Matalab $\frac{5+195}{2} = 100$. Total terms $n = \frac{195}{5} = 39$. Seedha multiply mar: Sum = $39 \times 100 = 3900$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Formula $S_n = \frac{n}{2}(2a + (n-1)d)$ time waste hai. Jab AP me $a$ aur $l$ pata ho, toh $S_n = n \times \text{Average}$ use kar.

Future Exam Takeaway: Sum of AP hamesha 'Number of terms $\times$ Middle Term (Average)' hota hai. Pen uthane ki zaroorat nahi padni chahiye!

questions.q: $x, y,$ and $z$ are distinct prime numbers where $x < y < z$. If $x + y + z = 70$, then what is the maximum possible value of $z$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Parity Property)

Dekh bhai, ye basic properties pe khelne wala question hai. Numbers ko dekh ke dar mat.

Pen-Free Observation: Teen prime numbers ka sum $70$ (Even) hai. Teen odd numbers ka sum kabhi even nahi ho sakta. Matalab ek prime lazmi taur par $2$ hoga!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Sabse chota prime $x = 2$ set kar diya. Bacha $y + z = 68$. $z$ ko maximum karna hai toh options se check kar. Agar $z = 67$ (prime), toh $y = 1$ (not prime, reject). Agar $z = 61$ (prime), toh $y = 7$ (prime, accept!). Done.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Prime number set me sirf $2$ hi ek akela even warrior hai. Ye SSC/CDS ka favourite trap hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Jab bhi 3 prime numbers ka sum Even diya ho, toh aankh band karke sabse chote number ko $2$ maan lena.

questions.q: In how many ways can the number $10800$ be written as a product of two co-prime factors?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Combinatorics)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... jab bhi co-prime factors puche, sidha base primes count karo, pure group uthane hote hain.

Pen-Free Observation: $10800$ me prime bases $2, 3$ aur $5$ aayenge. Co-prime factors banane ke liye pure-pure base ki family uthani padegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Number of ways = $2^{n-1}$, jahan $n$ distinct prime bases ka count hai. $10800 = 2^4 \times 3^3 \times 5^2$. Yahan $n=3$ bases hain ($2,3,5$). Formula me daal: $2^{3-1} = 2^2 = 4$ ways. Seedha hack!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Co-prime matlab HCF $1$. Yani ek prime factor ya toh poora group A me jayega ya poora group B me. Ye distribution of distinct items jaisa hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Number system me 'ways to express as co-prime product' pooche toh bas prime bases gino aur $2^{n-1}$ thop do.

questions.q: What is the sum of $1 \frac{1}{2} + 4 \frac{1}{6} + 7 \frac{1}{12} + 10 \frac{1}{20} \dots$ upto $20$ terms?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Series Splitting & Deviation)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... mixed fractions ki heavy series kabhi direct ek sath nahi kholni.

Pen-Free Observation: Integer part ($1, 4, 7\dots$) alag se AP bana raha hai aur fraction part ($\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{6}\dots$) ek Telescoping series hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Integers: $1 + 4 + 7 \dots 20$ terms tak. Sum = $\frac{20}{2}[2(1) + 19(3)] = 10 \times 59 = 590$.
Fractions: $\frac{1}{1 \times 2} + \frac{1}{2 \times 3} \dots 20$ terms tak. Sum = $\frac{n}{n+1} = \frac{20}{21}$.
Dono jodd de: $590 + \frac{20}{21} = \frac{12390 + 20}{21} = \frac{12410}{21}$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Mixed series ko split karna best approach hai. Telescoping $\frac{1}{k(k+1)} = \frac{1}{k} - \frac{1}{k+1}$ me first aur last term bachti hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Mixed fractions ki badi series hamesha Integer + Fraction me tod kar solve karni hai.

questions.q: What is the result when the sum of the digits of $(10^{15} + 1)$ is divided by $11$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... language ka ghatiya trap samajh.

Pen-Free Observation: Sawaal me dhokha hai! Sawaal number ko $11$ se divide karne ka nahi hai, uske 'Sum of digits' ko $11$ se divide karne ka hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $10^{15} + 1$ number dikhne me kaisa hoga? Ek $1$, uske beech me $14$ zeros, aur aakhiri me ek $1$. Is pure number ke digits ko jodega toh sum aayega $1 + 0 + \dots + 1 = 2$. Ab $2$ ko $11$ se divide karega toh Remainder $2$ hi aayega na mere bhai!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $10^n + 1$ form me sum of digits hamesha $2$ hi hota hai, chahe $n$ kuch bhi ho.

Future Exam Takeaway: Language ko dhyan se padho. 'Sum of digits' aur 'Number' me confuse mat hona.

questions.q: $846523X7Y$ is a 9 digit number which is divisible by $9$, and $Y-X=6$. Find the value of $\sqrt{2X+4Y}$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Digital Root Balancing)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... C9 method lagana hai, poora joddna time waste hai.

Pen-Free Observation: $9$ ka rule matlab Digital Sum $9$ hona chahiye. Sum nikalte waqt $9$ banne wale pairs wahin uda do.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Remaining digits ka sum: $8+6+2+3+7 = 26 \implies 8$. Matalab $8 + X + Y$ ko $9$ se katna hai. Yani $X+Y$ ki value ya toh $1$ hogi ya $10$.
Given: $Y - X = 6$. Agar $X+Y=1$ liya toh values negative aayengi.
Toh $X+Y = 10$ aur $-X+Y = 6$ solve kar. Jodd de: $2Y = 16 \implies Y=8$. Toh $X=2$.
Equation me daal: $\sqrt{2(2) + 4(8)} = \sqrt{4 + 32} = \sqrt{36} = 6$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): C9 method me sum chota karke simultaneous equation me ghusa do.

Future Exam Takeaway: Divisibility of $9$ dekhte hi sab digits joddne nahi baithna, $9$ ke multiples ko raaste me hi cancel karte jao.

questions.q: What is the sum of the digits of the sum of all factors of $100$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Formula Application)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... chota number hai, direct formula laga aur aage badh.

Pen-Free Observation: $100$ ke total factors ka sum direct formulae se jaldi aayega. Uske baad bas digits ko joddna hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $100 = 2^2 \times 5^2$.
Sum of factors = $\left(\frac{2^3 - 1}{2-1}\right) \times \left(\frac{5^3 - 1}{5-1}\right) = (7) \times (31) = 217$.
Sum of digits of $217 = 2 + 1 + 7 = 10$. Khatam.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $(2^0+2^1+2^2)(5^0+5^1+5^2)$ method se bhi expand kar sakta hai. $100$ ke liye easy rehta hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: CGL Mains me direct formula application ke upar ek chota step (like sum of digits) laga kar traps banate hain.

questions.q: $0.\overline{47} + 0.5\overline{03} - 0.\overline{39} \times 0.\overline{9} = ?$
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Fraction Base Scaling)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... ek magical property use karke sawaal todna hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Sabse badi trick ye hai ki $0.\overline{9}$ hamesha exact $1$ ke barabar hota hai! Equation ko complex banane ke liye use dala gaya hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Equation ko decode kar: $\frac{47}{99} + \frac{503-5}{990} - \frac{39}{99} \times 1$.
Pehle $\frac{47}{99}$ aur $\frac{39}{99}$ ko handle kar: $\frac{47-39}{99} = \frac{8}{99} = \frac{80}{990}$.
Ab isko second fraction me jodd de: $\frac{80}{990} + \frac{498}{990} = \frac{578}{990}$.
Wapas bar format me convert karne ke liye denominator me $990$ hai. Option A check kar: $0.5\overline{83} = \frac{583-5}{990} = \frac{578}{990}$. Matched!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Bar ko fraction me badalne ka rule: Puri sankhya minus bina bar wali sankhya, divided by jitne bar hain utne $9$ aur jitne khali utne $0$.

Future Exam Takeaway: $0.\overline{9} = 1$ is property pe direct MCQ banta hai.

questions.q: Which prime number is a mandatory factor of any $8$-digit number of the form $abcdabcd$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Repdigit Cyclicity)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Repetition patterns hamesha magical numbers ke multiple hote hain.

Pen-Free Observation: Pattern dekh bhai, $abcdabcd$. Yeh repetition $10001$ se multiply karne par hi aati hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $abcdabcd = abcd \times 10001$.
Aur ye baat rata hua hona chahiye ki $10001$ ka prime factorization $73 \times 137$ hota hai. Toh kisi bhi is form ke number ko $73$ compulsory divide karega. Options me $73$ hai, tick maar!

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $xyxy = xy \times 101$. $xyzxyz = xyz \times 1001$. Inke prime factors tips pe hone chahiye.

Future Exam Takeaway: Repetition multipliers ko hamesha dimag me print rakho, direct hit sawal aata hai.

questions.q: If $N = 77^{77^{77}}$ and $M = 33^{33^{33}}$, what is the unit digit of $N \times M$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Cyclicity of 4)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... power towers dekh ke ghabrana nahi hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Base digits $7$ aur $3$ hain. Unki power towers ajeeb lag rahi hain but essentially wo Odd numbers ki Odd power hain. Matalab power HAMESHA Odd hi rahegi.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Unit digit me sirf aakhri power $4$ se divide hoti hai.
$N$ me power $77^{\text{odd}}$. $77 \pmod 4 \equiv 1$. Toh $1^{\text{odd}} = 1$. Base power $1$ aayegi. $7^1 = 7$.
$M$ me power $33^{\text{odd}}$. $33 \pmod 4 \equiv 1$. Toh $1^{\text{odd}} = 1$. Base power $1$. $3^1 = 3$.
Unit digit = $7 \times 3 = 21 \implies 1$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Power tower $a^{b^c}$ me bas $b \pmod 4$ check kar liya karo aur uski power $c$ chala do.

Future Exam Takeaway: Power towers dekh ke ghabrana nahi, Modulo 4 Cyclicity hamesha bachayegi.

questions.q: What is the sum of all possible values of $a$ for which the 4-digit number $3a4b$ is divisible by $45$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Composite Base Balancing)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... $45$ ka divisibility rule $5$ aur $9$ me tootega.

Pen-Free Observation: $5$ ke liye aakhri digit ($b$) ya toh $0$ hoga ya $5$.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
Case 1: Agar $b = 0$, number hai $3a40$. $9$ ka rule (sum of digits): $7+a$. $9$ se divide hone ke liye $a$ ko $2$ hona padega.
Case 2: Agar $b = 5$, number hai $3a45$. $9$ ka rule: $12+a$. $18$ banne ke liye $a$ ko $6$ hona padega.
Possible values of a ka sum = $2 + 6 = 8$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Pehle unit digit wale primes ($2, 5, 10$) fix karo, fir sum wale ($3, 9, 11$) apply karo.

Future Exam Takeaway: Composite divisors hamesha co-prime rules ($5 \times 9$) pe toote hain. Unit digit locking hamesha pehla step hona chahiye.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $55^{55}$ is divided by $7$.
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Negative Remainder)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... base ko divisor ke mutabik scale karo.

Pen-Free Observation: Base $55$ ko divisor $7$ ke paas la. $7 \times 8 = 56$. Toh $55$ negative remainder $-1$ dega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $55 \pmod 7 \equiv -1$.
Expression ban gaya $(-1)^{55}$.
Negative number ki Odd power ka result hamesha negative $(-1)$ hi hota hai.
Lekin remainder negative chhod nahi sakte. Isliye divisor ko add karke positive bana lo: $-1 + 7 = 6$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fermat's Theorem ki zaroorat nahi. Direct negative remainder is the fastest way.

Future Exam Takeaway: Hamesha base ko divisor ke multiple ke $\pm 1$ ke range me set karne ki koshish karo.

questions.q: Three fractions $x, y$ and $z$, are such that $x > y > z$. When the smallest of them is divided by the greatest, the result is $9/16$, which exceeds $y$ by $0.0625$. If $x+y+z = 1 \frac{13}{24}$ then the value of $x+z$ is:
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Fraction Decoding)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Language me extra details ko ignore karke direct fraction attack karo.

Pen-Free Observation: Main loop hai $0.0625$ ko decode karna, jo directly $\frac{1}{16}$ ka fraction value hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Question kehta hai ki $\frac{z}{x} = \frac{9}{16}$ aur ye $y$ se $\frac{1}{16}$ zyada hai.
Yani $y = \frac{9}{16} - \frac{1}{16} = \frac{8}{16} = \frac{1}{2}$.
Sum diya hai: $x + y + z = \frac{37}{24}$.
Hamein chahiye $x + z$. Toh seedha sum me se $y$ uda de!
$x + z = \frac{37}{24} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{37}{24} - \frac{12}{24} = \frac{25}{24}$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Fractions aur unki decimal values ($0.0625 = 1/16$) rata hona chahiye.

Future Exam Takeaway: Language chahe kitni ghumaye, fraction conversions dimag me ready rakho.

questions.q: What is the remainder when $(23^{(112^{717})} - 21^{(112^{717})})$ is divided by $88$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Algebraic Divisibility)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... gande powers humesha algebraic identity me fold hote hain.

Pen-Free Observation: Power check kar bhai, base $112$ even hai toh uski koi bhi power Even hi result degi. Matalab ye format $(x^n - y^n)$ hai jahan $n$ Even hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Jab $n$ even ho, toh $(x^n - y^n)$ compulsory $(x-y)$ aur $(x+y)$ dono se divide hota hai. Matlab $(x^2 - y^2)$ usko poora katega.
Yahan $x=23, y=21$.
$x^2 - y^2 = 23^2 - 21^2 = (23+21)(23-21) = 44 \times 2 = 88$.
Divisor bhi exact $88$ diya hai! Matalab number poori tarah kat jayega. Remainder seedha $0$ aayega.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Even powers create symmetric factors $(x+y)(x-y)$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Gande power towers hamesha Odd/Even check karne ke liye hote hain, calculate karne ke liye nahi.

questions.q: How many two-digit prime numbers are there between $10$ to $100$ which remain prime numbers when the order of their digits is reversed?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Static GK of Math)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Number system ke static facts sidhe memory se aate hain, prove nahi karne baithna.

Pen-Free Observation: Reverse karne par $2, 4, 5, 6, 8$ end me aane wale numbers even ya div by $5$ ban jate hain. Toh sirf $1, 3, 7, 9$ combinations matter karenge.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Wo primes list karo: $11, 13 (31), 17 (71), 37 (73), 79 (97)$.
Dhyan rakhna $19$ prime hai but ulta hoke $91$ banta hai jo $13 \times 7$ hota hai, toh wo out ho jayega.
Total count: $11, 13, 17, 31, 37, 71, 73, 79, 97$. Exact $9$ prime numbers hain.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Memory based check, specific digits ending logic reduce combinations.

Future Exam Takeaway: Kuch chize exam me prove nahi karni hoti, unhe as a static data treat karo.

questions.q: A number divided by $13$ leaves a remainder of $7$. The same number divided by $11$ leaves a remainder of $9$. What is the remainder when the same number is divided by $143$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (CRT Method)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... Jab do alag divisors aur remainders hon, toh Chinese Remainder Theorem lagti hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Divisors $13$ aur $11$ hain. Inka product hi final divisor $143$ diya gaya hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Badi condition pakdo: $N = 13k + 7$.
Values daal ke check kar. Agar $k=1$, toh $N = 20$.
Ab is $20$ ko second condition se check kar: $20 \div 11$, quotient $1$, remainder $9$. Perfect match!
Toh sabse chhota number $N = 20$ hi hoga.
Sawaal me $20 \div 143$ pucha hai, jiska remainder $20$ hi aayega.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): CRT me series banake (with the largest divisor) chote divisor se check karna faster hota hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: CRT wale sawalon me hamesha bade divisor ki series ($13k+7$) likh ke check karo.

questions.q: What are the last three digits of $3^{400}$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Binomial Expansion)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... jab digits zyada hon toh Binomial approach best hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Last $3$ digits nikalne ke liye format mod $1000$ hona chahiye. Base ko $10$ ke nazdeek todna padega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): $3^{400} = (3^4)^{100} = 81^{100}$.
Isko hum $(1 + 80)^{100}$ likh sakte hain.
Binomial expansion me last terms dekho: $\dots + \binom{100}{2}(1)^{98}(80)^2 + \binom{100}{1}(1)^{99}(80)^1 + \binom{100}{0}(1)^{100}(80)^0$.
Notice kar ki $80^2 = 6400$, aur isko jab $4950$ se multiply karenge toh aakhri me $3$ zeros ($000$) fix aayenge.
Toh sirf aakhri $2$ terms decide karenge: $100 \times 80 + 1 = 8001$.
Aakhri teen digit: $001$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Last 'k' digits maange toh expression ko hamesha $(1 \pm 10x)^n$ form me lana zaroori hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Tough digit extraction hamesha Binomial ke tail end (last 2-3 terms) se solve hoti hai.

questions.q: What are the last two digits of the product of the first $20$ odd prime numbers?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Modular Trap)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... options ka elimination aur modulo hack lagana padega.

Pen-Free Observation: Number 'odd primes' ka product hai. Yani isme ek baar $5$ aayega. Lekin ye number $25$ se divide nahi hoga kyunki prime set me dusra $5$ nahi hota. Toh last digits hargiz $25$ ya $75$ nahi ho sakte!

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Mod 4 and Mod 5 ka hack laga.
Product $P$ me $5$ nahi hai ($5$ alag rakh). Baaki primes ko Mod $4$ pe dekho.
Primes $\equiv 3 \pmod 4$ ki counting $11$ hogi pehle $20$ me. Unka product $(-1)^{11} \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.
Toh remaining product $P \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.
And $P \pmod 5$ calculate karne par $2$ aayega. CRT se $P = 4m+3 \equiv 2 \pmod 5 \implies m \equiv 1 \pmod 5$.
Toh last digits $5(20m+15)$. For $m=1$, value $= 35$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Ye highly logical CDS trap hai. Aapko pata hona chahiye ek single $5$ multiply hone par last 2 digit hamesha odd multiple of $5$ deta hai but not a multiple of $25$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Product of distinct primes kabhi bhi $25$ se divisible nahi hota, isliye wo kabhi $25$ ya $75$ par end nahi hoga.

questions.q: Evaluate: $0.23\overline{472} + 0.24\overline{362}$
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Direct Bar Expansion)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... fraction conversion mat lagana idhar, time waste ho jayega.

Pen-Free Observation: Fraction conversion $\frac{N}{99900}$ jaisi badsurat chize banati hain. Bar ko seedha expand kar ke add karna smartness hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach):
$0.23472472\dots$
$0.24362362\dots$
------------------
$0.47834834\dots$
Addition me $472 + 362 = 834$ sidha add ho raha hai bina kisi carry-forward (jo $>1000$ pe milta hai) ke. Iska matlab pattern perfectly $834$ ka hi banega.
Result = $0.47\overline{834}$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Carry check hamesha right se aane wale cycle pe kiya karo.

Future Exam Takeaway: Recurring decimals ko directly unki expanded form me likh ke basic addition karna sabse safe aur fast hai.

questions.q: What is the smallest positive number that must be added to the product of any two consecutive even numbers to make the result a perfect square?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Value Assumption)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... variables assume mat kar, seedha dummy values laga.

Pen-Free Observation: Seedha values assume kar lo. Pehle do even number $2$ aur $4$ man lo. Unka product $= 8$. Isme kya jode ki square bane? $+1$ karega toh $9$ ($3^2$) ban jayega.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Koi aur bada number lelo for safety: $10$ aur $12$. Product $= 120$. Isme kya jode ki perfect square bane? $121$ banane ke liye $+1$ karna hoga. Hamesha answer $1$ aayega.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Algebra se dekho: $x$ aur $(x+2)$ consecutive even numbers hain. Product $x^2 + 2x$ hota hai. Agar hum $+1$ kar dein, toh ye $(x+1)^2$ identity ban jayega.

Future Exam Takeaway: Variables $N, N+2$ wale statement sums humesha ek choti dummy value ($2,4$) le kar solve karne chahiye.

questions.q: Find the number of Zeros at the end of the product $(12 \times 27 \times 63 \times 113 \times 1250 \times 24 \times 650)$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Factor Hunting)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... zeros ka khel bottleneck pairs pe chalta hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Number of zeros utne hi hote hain jitne $2$ aur $5$ ke pairs banenge. Baki kachra numbers ($27, 63$) ignore marne hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Bas $5$ aur $2$ ki power gin!
Power of 5: $1250 = 5^4 \times 2$. $650 = 5^2 \times 26$. Total $5$ ki power = $4 + 2 = 6$.
Power of 2: $12 (2^2)$, $1250 (2^1)$, $24 (2^3)$, $650 (2^1)$. Total $2$ ki power = $2 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 7$.
Pair wahi banenge jo minimum power hogi. Minimum $(6, 7)$ me $6$ hai. Toh $6$ zeros lagenge end me.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Trailing zeros is entirely a game of bottleneck resource.

Future Exam Takeaway: Product form me hamesha 'botteneck variable' (usually $5$) ko extract karke direct tick maro, pura factorise mat karo.

questions.q: What is the remainder when the number $8888\dots$ (written $25$ times) is divided by $13$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Successive Change (Cycle Division)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... repdigits hamesha fixed cycle me cut hote hain.

Pen-Free Observation: $7, 11$, aur $13$ ka combined divisibility rule ek specific pattern create karta hai. Koi bhi ek digit ka number jab $6$ baar likha jaye ($aaaaaa$), wo $13$ se completely divide hota hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total $25$ digits hain. $6-6$ ki cycle me unhe uda de. $\frac{25}{6}$ ka remainder aayega $1$.
Matlab shuruwaat ke $24$ digits ($4$ pairs of $6$) mil kar perfectly zero remainder denge.
Bachega sirf aur sirf last ka aakhri $8$. Ab us akela $8$ ko $13$ se bhag dega toh remainder $8$ hi bachega.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $6$ times same digit is always divisible by $7, 11, 13, 37, 1001$.

Future Exam Takeaway: Repdigit questions ($7777\dots$) dekhte hi total digits ko $6$ se divide karke cycle choti kar lo.

questions.q: A book contains $500$ pages. How many times does the digit $3$ appear in the page numbers?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: Unitary Scaling (Block Counting Method)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... frequency counting hamesha blocks me karni chahiye.

Pen-Free Observation: Digit occurrence fixed pattern me chalti hai. Har $100$ ke block me tens aur unit digit ki fixed frequency milti hai.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Har standard block ($0-99, 100-199$ etc) me kisi bhi digit ka count exactly $20$ hota hai (in tens & unit places).
Range $1$ se $500$ me total $5$ block banenge. Toh $5 \times 20 = 100$ bar $3$ aayega.
Ab dhyan de 'Hundreds place' par: $300$ se leke $399$ tak, pure $100$ bar lagatar $3$ aayega.
Total jodd do: $100 + 100 = 200$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Base value calculate karke specific zone ke extra instances add karo.

Future Exam Takeaway: Digit frequency $0-99$ block me hamesha $20$ bar hoti hai, ye fact rat lo, calculation fast ho jayegi.

questions.q: Six bells commence tolling together at 7:59 am. They toll at intervals of $3, 6, 9, 12$ and $15$ seconds respectively. How many times will they toll together till 8:16 am? (excluding the toll at 7:59 am)
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (LCM Interval Scaling)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... interval wale question hamesha LCM se chalte hain.

Pen-Free Observation: LCM ka direct execution hai. Values $3, 6, 9, 12, 15$ choti hain, inka LCM mentally $180$ seconds aana chahiye.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): LCM of $3, 6, 9, 12, 15 = 180$ seconds = $3$ minute.
Time kitna available hai? 7:59 se 8:16 am tak total $17$ minute hain.
Har $3$ minute par toll hoti hai. Toh $17$ minute me kitni baar aayega? $17 \div 3 = 5$ times (ignoring the fraction).
Question ne directly 'excluding start toll' bola hai, toh $+1$ wali tension nahi leni. Answer exact $5$.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): Total Times = $\lfloor \frac{\text{Total Duration}}{\text{LCM}} \rfloor$. Agar initial include karne bole tab $+1$ hota hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: Traffic light aur Toll bell questions me language padh lena ki initial occurrence add karni hai ya minus.

questions.q: How many numbers are there between $1$ and $800$ which are divisible by $3$ and $7$ but not divisible by $9$?
questions.s:
Core Tool Triggered: JSM (Divisibility Venn Set)

Dekh bhai aise karna hai... overlap subtract karne ka Venn Diagram logic lagta hai.

Pen-Free Observation: Jo $3$ aur $7$ dono se divide honge wo inke LCM, yani $21$ se divide honge. Hamein unme se wo nikal dene hain jo $9$ ki gang se hain.

Method 1 (Ninja Technique / Exam Approach): Total numbers div by $21$ ($3$ & $7$): $\lfloor \frac{800}{21} \rfloor = 38$ numbers.
Numbers jo $21$ aur $9$ dono se divide ho, wo LCM of $(21,9) = 63$ ke under aayenge.
Unki counting: $\lfloor \frac{800}{63} \rfloor = 12$ numbers.
Hame subtract kar dena hai: $38 - 12 = 26$. Options match.

Method 2 (Concept Builder): $n(A \cap B) - n(A \cap B \cap C)$ ka standard set theory format lag raha hai.

Future Exam Takeaway: 'But NOT divisible by' jab bhi aaye, dono target values ke LCM se range ko divide kar ke original me se ghata diya karo.
